demo_flow.tip: Start with a relatable scenario, not a technical description
Mention design thinking and key decisions briefly
LIVE DEMO — one complete user journey, narrate as you click
Run a test case live, acknowledge limitations honestly
What surprised you, future scope, end on a strong note
Keep answers under 20 seconds, don't bluff

jury_pitch_template: We built [SOLUTION NAME] to help [TARGET USER] with [PROBLEM]. Our approach uses [KEY TECHNOLOGY/METHOD] to [CORE VALUE]. In our demo, you'll see [ONE USER JOURNEY]. We validated with [N] test cases. If we had more time, we'd add [FUTURE FEATURE]. Key insight: [LEARNING].

common_jury_questions.q: How is this different from ChatGPT?
common_jury_questions.a: Curated knowledge base, enforced guardrails, structured output — not generic LLM chat.

common_jury_questions.q: What if the AI gives bad advice?
common_jury_questions.a: Guides not solves, assumptions tagged, fallback to rule-based. Team still decides.

common_jury_questions.q: What if the AI is unavailable?
common_jury_questions.a: Timeout detection, keyword-matched fallback, generic template. Same schema always.
Future: multi-session memory, skill calibration, voice. Current scope: single-session demo.
Contract-first: locked JSON schema, each built against stubs, integrated at checkpoint.
Be genuine — scoping to 90 min, consistent AI output, edge cases.
